title: The Project Timeline
description: GET /v1/timeline. A Project's deliveries in the order they happened, and — for each — what this Mac can actually prove about it. The whole reason the feature exists is that a commit, a build, a task that said `success` and an assistant's summary are none of them evidence that something is available to anybody (design-decisions D41, timeline-design A1). This daemon has no producer of deployment evidence, so nothing here is ever drawn as available: an entry is `landed_to_git` when the broker's landing record proves a commit reached its target, and `upcoming` when a delivery has not landed. It is a projection and stores nothing of its own (D01, D04).

TimelineStatus.description: What this Mac can prove about one entry. Only the three this daemon can reach are here: the Swift app's other nine name deployment outcomes, and a word no producer can ever write is a promise the screen cannot keep (design-decisions X25).

TimelineCategory.description: What kind of work an entry was. `feature` for ordinary delivery, `operation` for a task whose write set was only tooling or documentation.

TimelineHistoryStatus.description: How far back this Project's coverage reaches. `unknown` is the honest answer while no history importer exists; `capacity` is the entry bound reached, and what was retained is never removed to make room.

label.description: The repository's own name. Never a reconstruction of one this Mac no longer holds.

TimelineRevision.description: One commit an entry rests on, as the landing record proved it. `githubUrl` only when the repository is a GitHub one this daemon can name with certainty.

TimelineEvent.description: One piece of evidence under an entry, and who said it. `authority` is what wrote it down — `broker` for this daemon's own landing record — because an event with no authority is an assertion.

effectiveAt.description: Unix seconds: when the thing happened. Absent when only the observation time is known.

observedAt.description: Unix seconds: when this Mac learned of it.

TimelineProjection.description: What the events below add up to. `availableTargets` is how many targets this entry is proved available on, which on this daemon is always zero: there is no deployment evidence producer, and a required target nothing can answer is not the same as a failure.

effectiveAt.description: Unix seconds. Absent when nothing under this entry carried one.

TimelineEntry.description: One delivery. The id is the broker task's, because the task is the thing that was delivered and an id of this projection's own invention would be a second name for it.

boardItemIds.description: The work items this delivery is on, as the task's own `work_id` names them.

originalTitle.description: The task's own title, never a summary written for it.

summary.description: The delivery's own one-paragraph account of itself, cut to a length the card can hold. Absent when the task wrote none.

TimelineCheckpoint.description: How far one Project's history has been read. It is derived on every read and stored nowhere, so it can never freeze the way a saved cursor did.

TimelineCapacity.description: The entry bound, on the wire where a reader can see it (timeline-design A4). What is dropped at the bound is the oldest, and it is a projection of records this daemon still holds, so nothing is lost by dropping it.

canManage.description: False on this daemon, always: the Timeline is a projection of records it already keeps, so there is no switch to turn it off and nothing a viewer could manage.

nextCursor.description: A keyset cursor — the last entry's time and id — not an offset, so a page that arrives while records are being written cannot skip an entry (timeline-design A5). Absent on the last page.

revision.description: The reading's own counter. It changes when the records under it do; nothing writes to this projection, so it is never a compare-and-set token.

status.description: `current`, or `partial` when one of the sources under this reading could not be read — never an empty list drawn as a quiet Project.
